title: Mental Health Practice
description: Inquiries, clients, sessions with note status, and statements for a counseling practice.

spec.useCase: Lowell Prescott administers a small counseling practice and uses this to answer inquiries within a day, run each clinician's session schedule, make sure notes get finished and chase unpaid statements.

text.text: Your practice in one place. Start with Inquiries to reply to today, then Sessions for the day's schedule and unfinished notes, and Statements for payments. Operational tracking only; clinical notes and records stay in your clinical record system.
A prompt, warm reply matters. Keep messages short and follow your own privacy practices.
Log the inquiry and set Reply by to the next business day.
Reply with availability, fees and how intake works.
If the practice is full, offer the Waitlist and say how long it usually takes.
When it is not a fit
Share two or three referral options and mark the inquiry Not a fit.
Consent, privacy notice and fee agreement signed
Unfinished notes pile up fast. Review every Friday.
Open Sessions and filter Note status Not started and Drafted.
Each clinician finishes their own and sets Signed.
The administrator sends a gentle reminder for anything older than a week.
Only the status lives here. The note itself stays in your clinical record system.
Create one statement per client from the completed sessions.
Send it the way the client prefers and mark it Sent.
Mark it Paid as payments arrive.
After the due date, mark it Overdue and send a short, kind reminder.
After two reminders, the clinician decides on next steps.
